title: Hedged Capacity Playbook & Policy-driven Autoscale Runway (Q2 pilot)
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: Create a pragmatic, testable playbook that lets Dedicated customers opt into a ‘hedged capacity’ runway for short-term demand spikes while preserving cost predictability. This project combines policy-driven autoscale lanes, a smoothing buffer (soft-reserve), and a canary rollout pattern to validate customer-facing behavior and cost telemetry.

Problem statement: Dedicated pools face two competing needs — keep latency SLOs through bursts, and avoid high unit cost from always-on overprovisioning. Existing autoscale mechanisms either react too slowly for 95th/99th percentile spikes or force customers to buy larger reserves. We propose a hedged runway that pre-allocates small timed buffers with automatic policy fallbacks.

Scope:
- Define policy primitives (priority lanes, hedged-window sizes, backfill tolerances).
- Implement control-plane flags and API schema for customers to opt into hedged windows.
- Design canary workflow for Q2 pilot with three customers (internal + 2 beta).
- Observability: add telemetry for hedge-fill-rate, latency impact, cost delta per hedge-window.
- Runbook: operator steps for manual intervention and rollback criteria.

Out of scope: full productized pricing model changes, multi-region scheduling optimizations (deferred to a follow-up).

Approach:
1) Product design: draft policy definitions and UX for Console and API.
2) Eng prototype: lightweight control-plane gating and autoscaler hook into existing Dedicated autoscale policies.
3) Pilot: enroll 3 customers for 6-week trial; track SLOs and cost.
4) Iterate: tighten policy defaults, add rollback triggers, prepare docs and billing notes.

Milestones:
- Feb 10: Finalized policy spec and Console mockups.
- Feb 24: Eng prototype merged behind feature flag.
- Mar 2: Internal canary + smoke tests.
- Mar 16: Beta customer onboarding.
- Apr 7: Pilot completion + metrics review.

Success metrics:
- Maintain 99th percentile latency within SLO for pilot customers.
- Reduce committed-reserve overprovision for pilot customers by >= 18% without increasing cost per token beyond 6%.
- Hedge fill-rate >= 60% for detected burst events (i.e., buffer used rather than fallback to high-cost reserve).

Trade-offs & notes:
- Hedge windows accept small increased bookkeeping in exchange for fewer large reservations.
- Early default parameters favor reliability (larger hedges) to avoid regressions; cost tuning will come after pilot.

Control-plane flag and API schema merged behind feature flag
Telemetry dashboard with baseline and pilot panels available
Canary run executed internally with no SLO regressions
Pilot customers onboarded and 6-week trial initiated
risks: If hedge fills are low, customers may experience more fallbacks than expected leading to cost spikes
Miscommunication on billing could drive adverse customer support cases
Edge-case interactions with Dedicated reservation hedges in multi-tenant scheduling
decisions: Default hedge window set to 15 minutes for pilot (balances responsiveness and cost).
Pilot will use opt-in model with explicit billing notice (no auto-enrollment).
Rollback criteria: two sequential severe latency regressions (above 150% of SLO) or sustained cost delta >10% over two weeks.
